title: Goal of the game
text: Chess is won by checkmating the opposing king: the king is attacked and has no legal escape. Capturing the king is not a legal move.

title: Starting position
text: Each side starts with eight pawns, two rooks, two knights, two bishops, one queen, and one king. White moves first.

title: Taking turns
text: White and Black alternate one move at a time. A player may not pass a turn.

title: King movement
text: A king moves one square in any direction, but it may not move onto a square attacked by an opposing piece.

title: Queen movement
text: A queen moves any number of unobstructed squares along a rank, file, or diagonal.

title: Rook movement
text: A rook moves any number of unobstructed squares along a rank or file.

title: Bishop movement
text: A bishop moves any number of unobstructed squares diagonally and remains on the same color of square.

title: Knight movement
text: A knight moves in an L shape: two squares in one orthogonal direction and one perpendicular square. It may jump over pieces.

title: Pawn movement
text: A pawn moves one square straight forward into an empty square. From its starting rank it may move two empty squares; pawns capture one square diagonally forward.

title: Capturing a piece
text: A move captures an opposing piece by legally moving onto its occupied square. A player may not capture a friendly piece.

title: Responding to check
text: A player whose king is in check must make a legal move that removes every attack on the king. A player may not leave or move their own king in check.

title: Checkmate
text: Checkmate occurs when a king is attacked and the player has no legal move that removes the attack. The attacking player wins immediately.

title: Stalemate
text: Stalemate is a draw when the player to move is not in check but has no legal move.

title: Castling requirements
text: Castling moves the king two squares toward a rook and places that rook beside the king. The king and that rook must not have moved, and the squares between them must be empty.

title: Castling and attacked squares
text: Castling is illegal while the king is in check, through a square attacked by an opponent, or onto an attacked square. An attacked rook square does not by itself prevent castling.

title: En passant
text: After an opposing pawn advances two squares from its starting rank and lands beside your pawn, your pawn may capture it as though it moved only one square. This option exists only on the immediately following move.

title: Pawn promotion
text: A pawn reaching the farthest rank must be replaced on that move by a queen, rook, bishop, or knight of the same color. The choice is not limited by pieces previously captured.

title: Draw by agreement
text: Players may agree to a draw during a game under the competition procedure. A draw offer cannot be withdrawn once made and remains valid until accepted, rejected, or followed by a move.

title: Threefold repetition
text: A player may claim a draw when the same position is about to appear three times or has just appeared for the third time, with the same player to move and the same possible moves.

title: Fifty-move rule
text: A player may claim a draw when each player has completed fifty moves without any pawn move or capture. The claim follows the competition procedure.

title: Dead position and insufficient material
text: The game is drawn when no possible legal sequence can lead to checkmate. Common insufficient-material examples include king against king and king plus a lone bishop or knight against king.

title: Seventy-five-move automatic draw
text: The game is automatically drawn after each player completes seventy-five moves without a pawn move or capture, unless the last move checkmates.

title: Fivefold repetition automatic draw
text: The game is automatically drawn when the same position occurs at least five times with the same player to move and the same possible moves.

title: Touch-move rule
text: In over-the-board competition, deliberately touching one of your pieces requires moving it if it has a legal move. Deliberately touching an opposing piece requires capturing it if legally possible.

title: Adjusting a piece
text: A player who clearly announces an intention to adjust a piece, commonly by saying j'adoube, may center it on its square without invoking touch-move.

title: Using a chess clock
text: A player presses their own clock after making a move, which starts the opponent's clock. A move is normally completed when the clock is pressed.

title: Illegal moves
text: An illegal move must be corrected according to the competition rules. Tournament penalties depend on the event format and the number of completed illegal moves.

title: Resignation
text: A player may resign, immediately giving the opponent the win, unless the position is one in which the opponent cannot possibly checkmate by any legal sequence.

title: Recording moves
text: In events requiring score sheets, players record their own and the opponent's moves in algebraic notation as prescribed by the competition rules.

title: Making a draw claim
text: A player claiming a draw under the fifty-move or threefold-repetition rule should follow the event procedure, which can include writing the intended move and stopping the clock before calling the arbiter.
